llm.summary: The skill's core purpose (plan and simulate session-only workflows) is coherent, but the SKILL.md also claims it will create cron jobs and thus persist scheduling on the host — contradicting the 'no persistence' guarantee and implying system-level changes that are not declared.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (build and simulate multi-step workflows) match the instructions: step building, dry-run simulation, API steps via built-in HTTP, and limited branching. However the 'Cron Integration' statement (agent creates a cron job that triggers the workflow) does not fit the stated session-only, non-persistent purpose and suggests additional capability not declared in requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md largely scopes actions to simulation and built-in HTTP calls, but it also instructs the agent to create cron jobs and 'execute' workflows using built-in tools and to 'send message / create reminder' without specifying targets or required integrations. Creating cron jobs implies modifying system crontab or scheduling subsystems (a file/system change) despite repeated claims that workflows are never written or persisted. That contradiction is scope creep and raises risk: the instructions give the agent authority to alter system scheduling without declaring it.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials, which aligns with a simulation-focused tool. But some runtime behaviors described (sending messages, integrating with external services, and creating cron jobs) would normally require credentials or system permissions; those are not declared. The omission is noteworthy and ought to be clarified.

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request persistent presence, but the 'Cron Integration' feature implies persistent changes (scheduled jobs) and possible modifications to system crontab. This conflicts with repeated claims of session-only non-persistence and is a real privilege escalation compared with the declared footprint.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill mostly does what it says (build and simulate workflows), but there is a clear contradiction: the documentation repeatedly says workflows are session-only and not persisted, yet also claims the agent will create cron jobs (which would persist and modify the host). Before installing or enabling this skill, ask the author to explicitly clarify: 1) Does the agent actually write to crontab or any system scheduler? If so, what exact commands/files are modified and what permissions are required? 2) How does 'send message / create reminder' work — which external services/endpoints are used and what credentials are needed? 3) Confirm that no data is exfiltrated and whether the agent will prompt for explicit user consent before making persistent changes. If you cannot get clear answers, run this skill only in a restricted sandbox or decline to install it, since the undocumented cron behavior could create persistent system changes beyond the stated scope.
